'''''Rumohra''''' is a [[genus]] of ferns in the family [[Dryopteridaceae]], subfamily [[Elaphoglossoideae]], in the [[Pteridophyte Phylogeny Group]] classification of 2016 (PPG I).<ref name=PPGI/>

The [[frond]]s of species within this genus contain round [[Sorus|sori]] (reproductive clusters) on the underside of the [[pinnation|pinnae]] (leaflets) unlike many other ferns which have separate specialized reproductive fronds. Many of the sori have [[Leaf shape|peltate]] indusia and have prominent scales on the [[stipe (botany)|stipe]]s of the fronds. Species have a wide distribution; for example, ''[[Rumohra adiantiformis]]'' is found in the [[Old World]] as well as the [[New World]], including such diverse places as the [[Galapagos Islands]]<ref name=Wigg71/> and New Zealand.
